extracted.intended_audience: graduate students (and advanced undergraduates) learning algebraic geometry; readers studying schemes, Proj, and graded rings
extracted.subtask_description: Core definitions, constructions, and tests for schemes (affine and projective), their structure sheaves, local properties (stalks, residue fields, fibers), gluing constructions, and the Proj construction from graded rings. Includes worked examples and exercises that show how to verify properties like affineness, separatedness, and global sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recover ring from an affine scheme (global sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (X, OX) is an affine scheme Spec A, then the ring of global sections recovers A: Γ(X, OX) = A (since X = D(1) and Γ(D(1), OSpec A) = A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the structure sheaf on an affine scheme: from X you can recover its ring by taking global sections; moreover one gets an isomorphism π : (Spec Γ(X, OX), OSpec Γ(X,OX)) ≅ (X, OX). Example: verify on points via maximal ideals. See Exercise 4.3.A for rigour about isomorphisms of Specs corresponding to ring isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bijectivity between scheme isomorphisms and ring isomorphisms (Spec)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe a bijection between isomorphisms Spec A → Spec A' and ring isomorphisms A' → A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hardest part: show two morphisms agreeing on points must be equal; then show equality as maps of topological spaces; then equality on structure sheaves using the distinguished base. See Exercise 4.3.A (ENLIGHTENING EXERCISE) for details and warnings about circularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affines and localization: D(f) ≅ Spec A_f
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the identification of D(f) in Spec A with Spec A_f there is a natural isomorphism of ringed spaces (D(f), OSpec A|D(f)) ≅ (Spec A_f, OSpec A_f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguished open sets of Spec A_f are already distinguished open sets in Spec A; use this to compare topologies and restriction of structure sheaf. See Exercise 4.3.B (IMPORTANT BUT EASY EXERCISE).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open subscheme criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a scheme and U is any open subset, then (U, OX|U) is also a scheme (an open subscheme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 4.3.3: such U are called open subschemes; when U is affine we call it an affine open. Example: D(f) is an affine open subscheme of Spec A. See Exercise 4.3.C and 4.3.D.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine opens form a basis for the Zariski topology
rubrics_metrics.description: In any scheme X the affine open sets form a basis for the Zariski topology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Exercise 4.3.D (EASY): use that every point has an affine neighborhood (by scheme definition) and that affine opens cover; this is used repeatedly for local computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disjoint union / coproduct behavior for schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: The disjoint union of schemes is the coproduct in the category of schemes; it is the set-theoretic disjoint union with expected topology and sheaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (a) Finite disjoint unions of affine schemes are affine. (b) An infinite disjoint union of (nonempty) affine schemes is not affine (affine schemes are quasicompact). See Exercise 4.3.E for proofs and hints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closed subschemes are scheme structures on closed subsets (nonuniqueness)
rubrics_metrics.description: A closed subset of a scheme can carry many distinct 'natural' scheme structures; closed subschemes are particular kinds of scheme structures on closed subsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Spec A/I gives a scheme structure on V(I), but different ideals (e.g., (x) and (x^2) in k[x]) can have the same vanishing set. Formal discussion postponed to Chapter 8 (see 8.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalks of the structure sheaf for affine schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: The stalk of OSpec A at the point [p] is the local ring A_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 4.3.F (IMPORTANT EASY EXERCISE): the same applies to sheaves of modules (Mp has stalk Mp). Consequence: a module is zero iff all its localizations at prime ideals are zero; sections determined by germs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally ringed space structure: values and residue fields
rubrics_metrics.description: A ringed space is locally ringed if its stalks are local rings; for a scheme X the maximal ideal at p is m_X,p and the residue field κ(p)=O_{X,p}/m_{X,p}; values of functions at p lie in κ(p), and a function vanishes at p iff its value is 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 4.3.6: this generalizes values of functions on Spec A. Notation and conventions for evaluating functions at points are given; caution that 'function vanishing' doesn't make sense for arbitrary ringed spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero locus and invertibility of functions on locally ringed spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For f a function on a locally ringed space X, the subset where f vanishes is closed. (b) If f vanishes nowhere on X then f is invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 4.3.G (USEFUL EXERCISE): Hint: show the subset where the germ of f is invertible is open; invertibility is local and characterized by nonvanishing of germ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Residue field at a point for affine schemes and commuting of localization & quotient
rubrics_metrics.description: For a point [p] in Spec A, the residue field κ([p]) is A_p / p A_p, isomorphic to K(A/p), the fraction field of A/p. Localization at p and taking quotient by p commute (diagram in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to compute values of rational functions at closed and generic points; examples illustrate that residue fields need not be algebraically closed even for finitely generated algebras over C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiber of an OX-module at a point
rubrics_metrics.description: For an OX-module F on a scheme X the fiber at p is F|_p := F_p ⊗_{O_{X,p}} κ(p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notion is important for later topics (see reference to 13.7); example: OX|_p = κ(p).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hartogs-type extension phenomenon in algebraic geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: Removing a closed subset of codimension at least 2 often does not create new global regular functions: e.g., any function on A^2 minus the origin extends to all of A^2 (analogue of Hartogs's Lemma).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 4.4.1 and Aside 4.4.2; more precise statement for normal schemes given later (Theorem 11.3.11). This explains why Γ(A^2 \ {0}, O) = k[x,y].

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for affineness via global sections and point-ideal correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: If U is affine and U ≅ Spec A, then A = Γ(U, O); to test affineness compute Γ(U,O) and check whether Spec Γ(U,O) matches U (e.g., prime ideal <-> point correspondence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the bijection between primes and points to find contradictions: Example A^2 \\ {0} is not affine because the prime (x,y) would have to correspond to a missing point. See 4.4.3 and Exercise 4.4.B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing schemes along isomorphic opens (existence and cocycle condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given schemes Xi and isomorphisms fij : Xij → Xji between specified open subschemes satisfying the cocycle condition fij ◦ fjk = fik on triple intersections (and fii = identity), there exists a unique (up to unique iso) scheme X obtained by gluing the Xi along this data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 4.4.A (ESSENTIAL EXERCISE): construct X as the quotient of the disjoint union with quotient topology and glue structure sheaves; check uniqueness and that resulting space is a scheme (each point has affine neighborhood).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and pathology: affine line with doubled origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Gluing two copies of A^1 along D(t) ≅ D(u) via t ↔ u yields the affine line with doubled origin, a scheme that fails a 'Hausdorff-like' condition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This example is used to motivate the notion of separatedness (to prevent doubled-origin phenomena). Use it to see why intersection of affine opens may fail to be affine in non-separated schemes; see Exercise 4.4.B and 4.4.C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective line via gluing and behavior of global functions
rubrics_metrics.description: P^1_k obtained by gluing two copies of A^1 along the overlap by t ↔ 1/u; global regular functions on P^1 are constants, Γ(P^1,O)=k, so P^1 is not affine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 4.4.6 and Proposition 4.4.8: to show non-affineness compute global sections and observe only constants survive the overlap conditions (polynomials in t that are polynomials in 1/t must be constants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of projective n-space by gluing n+1 affine patches
rubrics_metrics.description: P^n_k is built by gluing n+1 open sets Ui ≅ Spec k[x0/i, ..., xn/i]/(xi/i - 1) with identifications on overlaps D(xj/i) ↔ D(xi/j) given by xk/i = xk/j / xi/j, satisfying triple-overlap compatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 4.4.9 and Exercise 4.4.D: verify gluing relations and triple-overlap cocycle as in gluing general schemes. This local description yields coordinate charts and homogeneous coordinate intuition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric interpretation of Chinese Remainder Theorem via schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: Spec Z/60 decomposes into closed points corresponding to primes dividing 60 ((2),(3),(5)); global sections decompose as Z/60 ≅ Z/4 × Z/3 × Z/5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figure 4.8 and 4.4.11: think of global sections as tuples of sections on each connected (closed) component; nilpotents and stalks reflect local behavior (Z/4 at (2), etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-to-global gluing of rational/local expressions (analytic continuation analogue)
rubrics_metrics.description: A section can be given by different rational/local expressions on different open sets that agree on overlaps, but might have no single global rational expression f/g valid everywhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example 4.4.12: on X = Spec k[w,x,y,z]/(wz-xy) the function described locally as z/y on D(y) and x/w on D(w) glues to a global section but cannot be written as one expression in w,x,y,z everywhere (denominator issues lead to 0/0). This warns against assuming global rational presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proj construction: points are homogeneous primes not containing S+
rubrics_metrics.description: For a graded ring S (Z_{≥0}-graded), Proj S is constructed from homogeneous prime ideals that do not contain the irrelevant ideal S+; affine building blocks are Spec(((S_f))_0) for homogeneous f∈S+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivation: for S = A[x0,...,xn] this recovers projective space patches; ((S_f))_0 denotes the degree-0 part of the localized graded ring (S_{(f)}). This yields a scheme by gluing these affines as f varies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graded ring conventions: homogeneous ideals, irrelevant ideal, generation in degree 1
rubrics_metrics.description: A Z_{≥0}-graded ring S has S0 a subring, S+ = ⊕_{i>0} S_i is the irrelevant ideal. An ideal is homogeneous if generated by homogeneous elements; S is finitely generated over A=S0 if S+ is finitely generated or S generated by finitely many homogeneous elements; 'generated in degree 1' means generated as an A-algebra by S1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 4.5.C and 4.5.D justify properties: homogeneous ideals closed under sum, product, intersection, radical; localizations preserve grading; Noetherian equivalence with finite generation over S0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine pieces for Proj: ((S_f))_0 as coordinate rings of patches
rubrics_metrics.description: For homogeneous f, the localized graded ring (S_{(f)}) has a degree-0 piece ((S_{(f)}))_0; Spec of that degree-0 piece gives the affine chart for Proj S corresponding to f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to construct Proj simultaneously from all such f (instead of choosing patches); applied to S = k[x0,...,xn] and f = xi recovers the coordinate rings used in the elementary gluing of P^n (see (4.4.9.1)).
